themes.theme: Ban on Letting Agent Fees - Core Policy
themes.reason: States the chosen method of implementation (primary legislation) and that it must cohere with existing regulation, directly addressing why/how the intervention will be rolled out.

Explores a separate, longer-term policy on deposit burdens rather than explaining how the fee ban itself will be implemented; it is adjacent exploration rather than a pillar of the implementation argument.
Defines a key carve-out to the ban's scope (what charges remain permissible) which is central to how the ban will function in practice.
Defines further exceptions to the ban (tenant-caused charges, bespoke services), directly shaping how the intervention is delivered and its boundaries.
A narrow specific rule preventing circumvention of the ban; useful detail but not a foundational pillar of the implementation argument.
Addresses an unintended consequence (discrimination risk) and justifies retaining holding deposits, bearing on the costs/benefits of the chosen implementation approach.
Central to explaining how the ban will be enforced, including alternative structures (lead authority) considered and their costs/benefits, directly addressing the implementation mechanism.
Explains a key delivery mechanism (empowering tenants to self-enforce) intended to reduce burden on authorities, directly bearing on how the ban will be rolled out and its benefits.
Explores a specific enforcement mechanism (data sharing) as one of the explicit alternative/complementary methods for delivering effective enforcement.
Discusses alternative or additional regulatory methods (register, code of practice, training) and reasons for caution, directly addressing the 'other methods considered' point.
Details the specific penalty options (civil vs criminal, fine levels) with costs/benefits, central to how enforcement of the ban will actually operate.
